description:

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Tips? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

transcript.text: Early on June 19th, 2024, Milton officers in Washington waited for Jory Edwards Nelson in a Taco Bell parking lot, after a tipster claimed they were arranging a drug deal for an ounce of fentany at 420 in the morning. In addition to the alleged deal, Jory was wanted on warrants for possession of a controlled substance. As Jory stepped out to meet the tipster, officers closed in. Spotting them, he rushed back into the driver's seat, prompting Officer Eric Haney to grapple with him through the window to stop his escape. Officer Haney failed to stop Jory, who sped off, running over Haney's legs and breaking his right femur. With the only other officer aiding Haney, Jory escaped. After the incident, Officer Haney recalled the tire nearly crushing his head. He was rushed to the hospital for surgery on torn ligaments and severe tissue damage. With Jory now wanted for first-degree assault on an officer, nearby agencies launched a coordinated manhunt. While officers searched for Jory, the tipster reported something unbelievable. Jory called the tipster again, still eager to sell fentanyl. claiming to be less than 10 miles away in Kent, seemingly oblivious to the tipster's intentions. The tipster provided several phone numbers used to contact him. Investigators learned Jory was often seen near Kent apartment complexes, lived in his car, and may be armed. A Kent officer spotted a matching vehicle at the apartment complex but with different plates. After checking the vehicle's identification number, they confirmed it was Jory's, suggesting he had swapped license plates to avoid detection. Because of the vehicle's dark tint, the officer did not immediately realize Jory was in the driver's seat. After attempting to communicate through the window, Jory suddenly drove off. The unharmed officer gave Jory's direction of travel and began the pursuit, activating his body-worn camera only after his interaction with Jory. That's the car. The vehicle is Southbound 132. situation. He chose to physically resist two police officers. He chose to put the vehicle,
and drive, and use thousands of pounds of solid metal to break my bones, tear my ligaments, damage
my flesh, and kill my nerves. We've placed a donation link below this video for those wishing
to support Officer Haney and his family. News articles indicate in March of 2025, Jory pled guilty
to four of his five charges in a plea deal. His vehicular assault charge was dropped. Jory was sentenced to
100 months, or eight years and four months in prison. In Washington, offenders can earn up to a third
off their sentence for good behavior.
With jail credit and good time,
Jory could be released by January 2030.
Without these benefits,
his full sentence ends in July 23.
He's going.
